body.input: The robot gets our attention more.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: The robot, when you walk in your house,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: is more likely to get you to remember to do the things

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: that you asked it to do

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: because it's kind of got a physical presence.

body.input: You can avoid it if you don't like it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: It could see you're avoiding it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: There's a lot of power to being embodied.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: There will be embodied AIs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: They have great power and opportunity and potential.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: There will also be AIs that aren't embodied,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: that just are little software assistants

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: that help us with different things

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: Will they be conscious?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: There will be attempts to program them

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: to make them appear to be conscious.

body.input: We can already write programs that make it look like,

body.input: oh, what do you mean?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: Of course I'm aware that you're there, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: I mean, it's trivial to say stuff like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: It's easy to fool people,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: but does it actually have conscious experience like we do?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: Nobody has a clue how to do that yet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: That seems to be something that is beyond

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: what any of us knows, how to build now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: Will it have to have that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: I think you can get pretty far with a lot of stuff

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: without it.

body.input: Will we accord it rights?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: Well, that's more a political game

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: than it is a question of real consciousness.

body.input: Yeah, can you go to jail for turning off Alexa

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: is a question for an election maybe a few decades from now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: to be shipped to the next place

body.input: where it would get a paid appearance, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: Yeah, it's dark and almost comedic, if not absurd.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: So I've heard you speak about your journey in finding faith.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: Sure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: And how you discovered some wisdoms about life

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: and beyond from reading the Bible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: And I've also heard you say that you said scientists

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: too often assume that nothing exists

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: beyond what can be currently measured.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: So in some sense, this assumption enables

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: the near term scientific method,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: assuming that we can uncover the mysteries of this world

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: by the mechanisms of measurement that we currently have.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: But we easily forget that we've made this assumption.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: So what do you think we miss out on

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: by making that assumption that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: It's fine to limit the scientific method

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: to things we can measure and reason about and reproduce.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: That's fine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: I think we have to recognize that sometimes we scientists

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: also believe in things that happen historically.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: You know, like I believe the Holocaust happened.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: I can't prove events from past history scientifically.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: You prove it historically.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: You prove them with historical evidence, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: With the impact they had on people,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: with eyewitness testimony and things like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: So a good thinker recognizes that science

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: is one of many ways to get knowledge.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: It's not the only way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: And there's been some really bad philosophy

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: and bad thinking recently, you can call it scientism,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: where people say science is the only way to get to truth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: And it's not, it just isn't.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: There are other ways that work also,

body.input: and the heart and the mind and the soul here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: I think we see but through a glass dimly in this life,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

body.input: we see only a part of all there is to know.

body.input: There's something in you that comes alive

body.input: and knows that there's a truth there

metadata.title: Podcast: Rosalind Picard: Affective Computing, Emotion, Privacy, and Health | Lex Fridman Podcast #24

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: And I consider the first, really the first figure of the Enlightenment is Newton,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: not Locke, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: It's a scientist.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: He teaches us the laws of mechanics, like how does stuff work?

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: And people go, oh, wow, this is cool.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: I can use my mind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: I can discover truth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: Isn't that amazing?

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: And everything opens up once you do that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: Hey, if I can discover, if I understand the laws of motion,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: if I can understand truth in the world, how come I can't decide who I marry?

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: I mean, everything was fixed in those days.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: Everybody belonged to a guild.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: How come I can't decide who my political leader should be?

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: So it's all reason.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: It's all once you understand the efficacy of your own mind to understand truth,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: to understand reality, discover truth, not understand truth, discover it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: everything opens up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: Now you can take responsibility for your own life because now you have the tool to do it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: But we are living in an era where postmodernism tells us there is no truth,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: there is no reality, and our mind is useless anyway.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: Critical race theory tells us that you're determined by your race,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: and your race shapes everything, and your free will is meaningless,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: and your reason doesn't matter because reason is just shaped by your genes

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: and shaped by the color of your skin.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: It's the most racist theory of all.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: And you've got our friend at UC Irvine telling them,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: oh, your senses don't tell you anything about reality anyway.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: Reality is what it is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: So, you know, what's the purpose of reason?

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: It's to invent stuff, it's to make stuff up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: And what use is that? It's complete fantasy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: You've basically got every philosophical, intellectual voice in the culture

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: telling them their reason is impotent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: There's like a Steven Pinker who tries, and I love Pinker,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: and he's really good, and I love his books.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: But, you know, he needs to be stronger about this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: And there's a few people on kind of, there's a few people,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: partially in the intellectual dark web and otherwise, who are big on reason,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: but not consistent enough and not full understanding of what it means

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: or what it implies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: And then there's little old me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: And it's me against the world in a sense,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: because I'm not only willing to articulate the case for reason,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: but then what that implies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: It implies freedom, it implies capitalism,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: it implies taking personal responsibility over your own life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: And the other intellectual dark web people get to reason,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: and they're, oh, politics, you can be whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: No, you can't. You can't be a socialist and for reason.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: It doesn't actually, those are incompatible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: And you can't be a determinist and for reason.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: Reason and determinism don't go together.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: The whole point of reason is that it's an achievement,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: it requires effort, it requires engagement, it requires choice.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: So it is, it does feel like a little old me, because that's it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: The allies I have are allies among some libertarians over economics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: I have some allies in the intellectual dark web maybe over reason,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: but none of them are allies in the full sense.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: My allies are the other objectivists, but they're not a lot of us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: For people listening to this, for the few folks kind of listening to this

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: and thinking about the trajectory of their own life,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: I guess the takeaway is reason is a difficult project,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: but a project that's worthy of taking on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: Yeah, and I don't know if difficulty is the right word,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: because difficult sounds like it's, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: I have to push this boulder up a hill.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: It's not difficult in that sense.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: It's difficult in the sense that it requires energy and focus.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: It requires effort, but it's immediately rewarding.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: It's fun to do, and its rewards are immediate, pretty quick, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: It takes a while to undo all the garbage that you have,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: but we all have that I had that took me years and years and years

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: to get rid of certain concepts and certain emotions that I had

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: that didn't make any sense,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: but it takes a long time to fully integrate that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: So I don't want it to sound like it's a burden, like it's hard in that sense.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: It does require focus and energy,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: and I don't want it to sound like a Dr. Spock.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: I don't want it to sound like a Dr. Spock,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: and I don't think I do because I'm a pretty passionate guy,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: but I don't want it to appear like, oh, just forget about emotions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: Emotions are how you experience the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: You want to have strong emotions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: You want to live.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: You want to experience life strongly and passionately.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: You just need to know that emotions are not cognition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: It's another realm.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: It's like don't mix the realms.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: Think about outcomes and then experience them,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: and sometimes your emotions won't coincide with what you think should be,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: and that means there's still more integration to be done.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: It's been, I was a little starstruck early on,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: getting a little more comfortable now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: I believe it's gone.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: It's been a gift.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: but the passion radiates in a way that's just contagious and awe-inspiring.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: Thank you for everything you've done for this world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: It's truly an honor and a pleasure to talk to you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: Well, thank you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: My award is that if I've had an impact on you and people like you, wow.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: I mean, that's amazing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: and people that I would have never thought.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: and a mind that goes out and does something about it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: then you get the exponential growth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: I think these ideas, ideas of reason and individualism will always be at the heart of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

body.input: What we are doing is continuing the project of the Enlightenment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yaron Brook: Ayn Rand and the Philosophy of Objectivism | Lex Fridman Podcast #138

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: testing, and ultimately the sustainment of these systems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: And so our vision is really that when our astronauts are there around Mars, you're going

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: to have that entire digital library of the spacecraft, of its operations, all the test

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: data, all the test data and flight data from previous missions to be able to look and see

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: if there are anomalous conditions and tell the humans and potentially deal with that

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: before it becomes a bad situation and help the astronauts work through those kinds of

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: And it's not just dealing with problems as they come up, but also offering up opportunities

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: for additional exploration capability, for example.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: So that's the vision is that these are going to take the best of the human to respond to

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: changing circumstances and rely on the best of AI capabilities to monitor this almost

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: infinite number of data points and correlations of data points that humans frankly aren't

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: that good at.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: So how do you develop systems in space like this, whether it's Alexa in space or in general

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: any kind of control systems, any kind of intelligent systems when you can't really test stuff too

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: much out in space.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: It's very expensive to test stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: So how do you develop such systems?

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: Yeah, that's the beauty of this digital twin, if you will.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: And of course with Lockheed Martin, we've over the past five plus decades been refining

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: our knowledge of the space environment, of how materials behave, dynamics, the controls,

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: the radiation environments, all of these kinds of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: So we're able to create very sophisticated models.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: They're not perfect, but they're very good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: And so you can actually do a lot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: I spent part of my career simulating communication spacecraft, missile warning spacecraft, GPS

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: spacecraft in all kinds of scenarios and all kinds of environments.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: So this is really just taking that to the next level.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: The interesting thing is that now you're bringing into that loop a system, depending on how

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: it's developed, that may be non-deterministic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: It may be learning as it goes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: In fact, we anticipate that it will be learning as it goes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: And so that brings a whole new level of interest, I guess, into how do you do verification and

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: validation of these non-deterministic learning systems in scenarios that may go out of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: bounds or the envelope that you have initially designed them to.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: So it has this system in its intelligence has the same complexity, some of the same

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: complexity a human does.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: And it learns over time, it's unpredictable in certain kinds of ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: So you also have to model that when you're thinking about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: In your thoughts, is it possible to model the majority of situations, the important

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: aspects of situations here on earth and in space enough to test stuff?

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: Yeah, this is really an active area of research and we're actually funding university research

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: in a variety of places, including MIT.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: This is in the realm of trust and verification and validation of, I'd say, autonomous systems

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: in general and then as a subset of that, autonomous systems that incorporate artificial intelligence

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: capabilities.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: And this is not an easy problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: We're working with startup companies, we've got internal R&D, but our conviction is that

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: autonomy and more and more AI-enabled autonomy is going to be in everything that Lockheed

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: Martin develops and fields.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: And autonomy and AI are going to be retrofit into existing systems, they're going to be

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: part of the design for all of our future systems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: And so maybe I should take a step back and say the way we define autonomy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: So we talk about autonomy essentially a system that composes, selects, and then executes

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: decisions with varying levels of human intervention.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: And so you could think of no autonomy, so this is essentially the human doing the task.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: You can think of effectively partial autonomy where the human is in the loop, so making

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: decisions in every case about what the autonomous system can do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: Either in the cockpit or remotely.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: Or remotely, exactly, but still in that control loop.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: And then there's what you'd call supervisory autonomy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: So the autonomous system is doing most of the work, the human can intervene to stop

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: it or to change the direction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: And then ultimately full autonomy where the human is off the loop altogether.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: And for different types of missions want to have different levels of autonomy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: So now take that spectrum and this conviction that autonomy and more and more AI are in

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: everything that we develop.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: The kinds of things that Lockheed Martin does, a lot of times are safety of life critical

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: kinds of missions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: Think about aircraft, for example.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: And so we require and our customers require an extremely high level of confidence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: One that we're going to protect life, two that we're going to, that these systems will

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: behave in ways that their operators can understand.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: And so this gets into that whole field.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: Again, being able to verify and validate that the systems have been, they will operate the

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: way they're designed and the way they're expected.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: And furthermore, that they will do that in ways that can be explained and understood.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: And that is an extremely difficult challenge.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: So here's a difficult question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: I don't mean to bring this up, but I think it's a good case study that people are familiar

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: with the Boeing 737 Max commercial airplane has had two recent crashes where their flight

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: control software system failed and it's software.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: So I don't mean to speak about Boeing, but broadly speaking, we have this in the autonomous

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: vehicle space too, semi-autonomous.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: We have millions of lines of code software making decisions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: There is a little bit of a clash of cultures because software engineers don't have the

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: same culture of safety often that people who build systems like at Lockheed Martin do where

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: it has to be exceptionally safe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: You have to test this on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: So how do we get this right when software is making so many decisions?

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: And there's a lot of things that have to happen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: By and large, I think it starts with the culture, which is not necessarily something that A

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: is taught in school or B is something that would come...

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: Depending on what kind of software you're developing, it may not be relevant if you're

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: targeting ads or something like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: And by and large, not just Lockheed Martin, but certainly the aerospace industry as a

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: whole, has developed a culture that does focus on safety, safety of life, operational safety,

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: mission success.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: But as you note, these systems have gotten incredibly complex.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: And so they're to the point where it's almost impossible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: State space has become so huge that it's impossible to, or very difficult to do a systematic verification

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: across the entire set of potential ways that an aircraft could be flown, all the conditions

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: that could happen, all the potential failure scenarios.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: Now maybe that's soluble one day.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: Maybe when we have our quantum computers at our fingertips, we'll be able to actually

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: simulate across an entire, almost infinite state space.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: But today, there's a lot of work to really try to bound the system to make sure that

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: it behaves in predictable ways and then have this culture of continuous inquiry and skepticism

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: and questioning to say, did we really consider the right realm of possibilities?

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: Have we done the right range of testing?

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: Do we really understand, in this case, human and machine interactions, the human decision

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: process alongside the machine processes?

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: And so that's that culture that we call it the culture of mission success at Lockheed

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: Martin that really needs to be established.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: And it's something that people learn by living in it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: And it's something that has to be promulgated, and it's done from the highest levels at a

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: company like Lockheed Martin.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: and regulations, but I mean, AI is an incredible enabler, say within the walls of Lockheed

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: Martin in terms of improving production efficiency, helping engineers doing generative design,

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: improving logistics, driving down energy costs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: I mean, there are so many applications, but we're also very interested in some of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: elements of ethical application within Lockheed Martin.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: So we need to make sure that things like privacy is taken care of, that we do everything we

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: can to drive out bias in AI enabled kinds of systems, that we make sure that humans

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: are involved in decisions that we're not just delegating accountability to algorithms.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: And so for us, it all comes back, I talked about culture before and it comes back to

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: sort of the Lockheed Martin culture and our core values.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: And so it's pretty simple for us to do what's right, respect others, perform with excellence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: And now how do we tie that back to the ethical principles that will govern how AI is used

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: within Lockheed Martin?

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: And we actually have a world, so you might not know this, but they're actually awards

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: for ethics programs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: the things that our ethics team is working with our engineering team on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: One of the miracles to me, perhaps a layman, again, I was born in the Soviet Union, so

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: I have echoes, at least in my family history of World War II and the Cold War.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: Do you have a sense of why human civilization has not destroyed itself through nuclear war?

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: So nuclear deterrence and thinking about the future, does technology have a role to play

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: here and what does the long-term future of nuclear deterrence look like?

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: Yeah, this is one of those hard, hard questions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: And I should note that Lockheed Martin is both proud and privileged to play a part in

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: multiple legs of our nuclear and strategic deterrent systems like the Trident submarine

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: launch ballistic missiles.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: You talk about, is there still a possibility that the human race could destroy itself?

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: I'd say that possibility is real, but interestingly, in some sense, I think the strategic deterrence

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: have prevented the kinds of incredibly destructive world wars that we saw in the first half of

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: the 20th century.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: Now things have gotten more complicated since that time and since the Cold War.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: It is more of a multipolar great powers world today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: Just to give you an example, back then there were in the Cold War timeframe just a handful

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: of nations that had ballistic missile capability.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: By last count, and this is a few years old, there's over 70 nations today that have that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: similar kinds of numbers in terms of space-based capabilities.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: So the world has gotten more complex and more challenging and the threats I think have proliferated

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: in ways that we didn't expect.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: The nation today is in the middle of a recapitalization of our strategic deterrent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: I look at that as one of the most important things that our nation can do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: What is involved in deterrence?

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: Is it being ready to attack or is it the defensive systems that catch attacks?

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: A little bit of both.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: It's a complicated game theoretical kind of program, but ultimately we are trying to prevent

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: the use of any of these weapons.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: The theory behind prevention is that even if an adversary uses a weapon against you,

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: you have the capability to essentially strike back and do harm to them that's unacceptable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: So that will deter them from making use of these weapons systems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: The deterrence calculus has changed of course with more nations now having these kinds of

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: weapons.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: But I think from my perspective, it's very important to maintain a strategic deterrent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: You have to have systems that you know will work when they're required to work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: You know that they have to be adaptable to a variety of different scenarios in today's

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: And so that's what this recapitalization of systems that were built over previous decades

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: making sure that they are appropriate not just for today, but for the decades to come.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: So the other thing I'd really like to note is strategic deterrence has a very different

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: character today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: We used to think of weapons of mass destruction in terms of nuclear, chemical, biological.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: And today we have a cyber threat.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: We've seen examples of the use of cyber weaponry.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: And if you think about the possibilities of using cyber capabilities or an adversary attacking

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: the US to take out things like critical infrastructure, electrical grids, water systems, those are

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: scenarios that are strategic in nature to the survival of a nation as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

body.input: So that is the kind of world that we live in today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Keoki Jackson: Lockheed Martin | Lex Fridman Podcast #33

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: in lots of different places, and this provides a much safer

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: model, and it provides value semantics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: everything is expensive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: And strings in Java are immutable,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: and there's optimizations for short ones,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: and it's complicated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: So you have to go allocate a third thing.

body.input: Because of the beauty of how the Swift value

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Yeah, OK.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Yeah, let's talk about this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: So I like how you put that, by the way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Well, I've listened to you enough.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: I'm a fan of yours, and I've listened to way too many

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Oh, yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: So I would argue that Python has one type.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Now, here are their trade-offs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Because it depends on what you're optimizing for.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: And Python is a super successful language

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: for a really good reason.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Because it has one type, you get duck typing for free

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: and things like this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: But also, you're making it very easy to pound out code,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: on the one hand.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: But you're also making it very easy to introduce

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: complicated bugs that you have to debug.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: And you pass a string into something

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: And it blows up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: And you're just saying, well, what did I do wrong?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: And so types are good and bad.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: And they have trade-offs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: They're good for performance and certain other things,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: depending on where you're coming from.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: But it's all about trade-offs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: And so this is what design is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: But also, within many types, how powerful

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: It's very interesting, by the way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131
