metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Before I ask it, let me say, with Python,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: I remember when I saw Lisp Comprehensions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Was like, when I really took it in.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: I don't know, I just loved it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: It was fun to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: It was fun to do that kind of,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: something about it, to be able to filter through a list,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: and to create a new list all in a single line was elegant.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: I could all get into my head, and it just made me

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: fall in love with the language.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: So is there, let me ask you a question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Is there, what do you use the most beautiful feature

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: in a programming language that you've ever encountered?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: In Swift, maybe, and then outside of Swift?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: I think the thing that I like the most

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: from a programming language,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: so I think the thing you have to think about

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: with a programming language, again, what is the goal?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: You're trying to get people to get things done quickly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: And so you need libraries, you need high quality libraries,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: and then you need a user base around them

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: that can assemble them and do cool things with them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: And so to me, the question is,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: what enables high quality libraries?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Okay. Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: And there's a huge divide in the world

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: between libraries who enable high quality libraries

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: versus the ones that put special stuff in the language.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: So programming languages that enable

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: high quality libraries. High quality libraries, got it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: So what I mean by that is expressive libraries

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: that then feel like a natural integrated part

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: of the language itself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: So an example of this in Swift is that int and float,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: and also array and string, things like this,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: these are all part of the library.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Like int is not hard-coded into Swift.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: And so what that means is that

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: because int is just a library thing

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: defined in the standard library,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: along with strings and arrays and all the other things

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: that come with the standard library,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: well, hopefully you do like int,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: but anything that any language features

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: that you needed to define int,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: you can also use in your own types.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: So if you wanted to find a quaternion

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: or something like this, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Well, it doesn't come in the standard library.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: There's a very special set of people

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: that care a lot about this,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: but those people are also important.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: It's not about classism, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: It's not about the people who care about ints and fluids

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: are more important than the people who care about quaternions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: And so to me, the beautiful things about programming

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: languages is when you allow those communities

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: to build high-quality libraries that feel native,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: that feel like they're built into the compiler

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: without having to be.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: What does it mean for the int to be part of not hard-coded in?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: So is it like, so what is an int?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Okay, int is just a integer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: In this case, it's like a 64-bit integer

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: or something like this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: So like the 64-bit is hard-coded or no?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: No, none of that's hard-coded.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: So int, if you go look at how it's implemented,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: it's just a struct in Swift.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: And so it's a struct.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: And then how do you add two structs?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Well, you define plus.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: And so you can define plus on int.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Well, you can define plus on your thing too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: You can define int as like an is odd method

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: or something like that on it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: And so, yeah, you can add methods on things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: So you can define operators, like how it behaves.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: That to you is beautiful when there's something

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: about the language which enables others to create libraries

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: which are not hacky.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Yeah, they feel native.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: And so one of the best examples of this is Lisp, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Because in Lisp, all the libraries

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: are basically part of the language, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: You write term rewrite systems and things like this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: And so can you, as a counter example, provide

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: what makes it difficult to write a library that's native?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Is it the Python C?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Well, so one example, I'll give you two examples.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Java and C++, or Java and C.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: They both allow you to define your own types.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: But int is hard coded in the language.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Okay, well, why?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Well, in Java, for example, coming back

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: to this whole reference semantic value semantic thing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: int gets passed around by value.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Yeah, that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: But if you make a pair or something like that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: a complex number, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: It's a class in Java, and now it gets passed around

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: by reference, by pointer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: And so now you lose value semantics, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: You lost math.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Okay, well, that's not great, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: If you can do something with int,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: why can't I do it with my type?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Right, so that's the negative side

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: of the thing I find beautiful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Is when you can solve that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: when you can have full expressivity,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: where you as a user of the language have as much

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: or almost as much power as the people

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: who implemented all the standard built-in stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Because what that enables is that enables

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: truly beautiful libraries.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: You know, it's kind of weird

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: because I've gotten used to that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: That's one, I guess, other aspect

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: of program language design.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: You have to think, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: the old first principles thinking,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: like, why are we doing it this way?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: By the way, I mean, I remember,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: because I was thinking about the Wallace operator,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: and I'll ask you about it later,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: but it hit me that like the equal sign for assignment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Like, why are we using the equal sign for assignment?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: It's wrong, yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: And that's not the only solution, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: So if you look at Pascal, they use colon equals

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: for assignment and equals for equality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: And they use like less than greater than

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: instead of the not equal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Like, there are other answers here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: So, but like, and yeah, like I ask you all,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: but how do you then decide to break convention to say,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: you know what, everybody's doing it wrong.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: We're gonna do it right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: So it's like an ROI, like return on investment trade-off,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: right, so if you do something weird,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: let's just say like not, like colon equal

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: instead of equal for assignment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: That would be weird with today's aesthetic, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: And so you'd say, cool, this is theoretically better,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: but is it better in which ways?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Like, what do I get out of that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Do I define away class of bugs?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Well, one of the class of bugs that C has

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: is that you can use like, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: if X equals without equals equals if X equals Y.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Right, well, turns out you can solve that problem

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: in lots of ways, Clang, for example, GCC,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: all these compilers will detect that as a,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: as a likely bug, produce a warning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Do they?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: I feel like they didn't, or Clang doesn't.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: They didn't.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: GCC didn't, and it's like, one of the important things

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: about programming language design is like,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: you're literally creating suffering in the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Like, I feel like, I mean, one way to see it

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: is the bicycle for the mind, but the other way

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: is to like, minimizing suffering.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Well, you have to decide if it's worth it, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: And so let's come back to that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Let's try to paint the big picture

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: so that then we can zero in on the individual steps

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: and make sure that we're making good progress.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: And so the Swift concurrency manifesto

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: is something I wrote three years ago.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: It's been a while, maybe more.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Trying to do that for Swift and concurrency.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: It starts with some fairly simple things

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: like making the observation that

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: when you have multiple different computers

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: or multiple different threads that are communicating,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: it's best for them to be asynchronous.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: And so you need things to be able to run separately

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: and then communicate with each other.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: And this means asynchrony.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: And this means that you need a way

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: to modeling asynchronous communication.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Many languages have features like this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Async await is a popular one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: And so that's what I think is very likely in Swift.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: But as you start building this tower of abstractions,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: it's not just about how do you write this?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: You then reach into the, how do you get memory safety?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Because you want correctness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: You want debuggability and sanity for developers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: And how do you get that memory safety into the language?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: So if you take a language like Go or C

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: or any of these languages,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: you get what's called a race condition

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: when two different threads or Go routines or whatever

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: touch the same point in memory, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: This is a huge maddening problem to debug

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: because it's not reproducible generally.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: And so there's tools, there's a whole ecosystem

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: of solutions that built up around this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: But it's a huge problem when you're writing concurrent code.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: And so with Swift, this whole value semantics thing

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: is really powerful there because it turns out that math

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: and copies actually work even in concurrent worlds.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: And so you get a lot of safety just out of the box,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: but there are also some hard problems

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: and it talks about some of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: When you start building up to the next level up

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: and you start talking beyond memory safety,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: you have to talk about what is the programmer model?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: How does a human think about this?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: So a developer that's trying to build a program

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: to think about this and it proposes a really old model

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: with a new spin called Actors.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Actors are about saying we have islands

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: of single threadedness logically.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: So you write something that feels like it's one programming,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: one program running in a unit,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: and then it communicates asynchronously with other things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: And so making that expressive and natural feel good,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: be the first thing you reach for

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: and it being safe by default is a big part of the design

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: of that proposal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: When you start going beyond that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: now you start to say, cool,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: well, these things that communicate asynchronously,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: they don't have to share memory.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Well, if they don't have to share memory

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: and they're sending messages to each other,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: why do they have to be in the same process?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: These things should be able to be in different processes

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: on your machine and why just processes?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Well, why not different machines?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: And so now you have a very nice gradual transition

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: towards distributed programming.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: And of course, when you start talking about the big future,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: the manifesto doesn't go into it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: but accelerators are things you talk to asynchronously

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: And how do you program those?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Well, that gets very interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: That's not in the proposal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: And how much do you wanna make that explicit,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: like the control of that whole process

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: explicit to the program?

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: Yeah, good question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: So when you're designing any of these kinds of features

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

body.input: or language features or even libraries,

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

metadata.title: Podcast: Chris Lattner: The Future of Computing and Programming Languages | Lex Fridman Podcast #131

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: she's attracting men who are of a different mate value

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: than she previously did.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Well, that triggers jealousy in the guy.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Even if she swears she's going to be totally loyal

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: and she has no signs of leaving or no signs of infidelity,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: a mate value discrepancy is going to trigger jealousy.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Now, what can it do?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Well, it can do, in the broadest sense,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: people can do two classes of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: They can do cost-inflicting things or benefit-providing things.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: So the man in that situation might say,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: okay, I need to devote more attention to my partner.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: I need to up my game when it comes to resource acquisition.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: I need to lavish more attention and gifts on her.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And so there's a whole suite of benefit-provisioning things

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: that can help to reduce that mate value discrepancy.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And then there's also cost-inflicting things.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And humans, unfortunately, do both sets of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Yeah, there's also this, maybe that's love.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: I notice the people I especially love or have a connection to,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: romantically or otherwise,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: there's a feeling like I don't deserve you.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: So with friends, with so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: I mean, I tend to think that about almost everything,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: which is why it's a strong signal when I don't feel it that way,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: which is like, how lucky am I to have this?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And that's a weird illusion of inflation of value or something.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: I think that the positive effect of that motivates me to be better.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: I guess on this 1 to 10 scale, to be higher.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And you sort of kind of have to...

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: It's a nice feature that your mind sees others that you have affection towards

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: as higher value, and it forces you to have that.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Like I'm a person that experiences jealousy,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: and that forces me to be better, to get my shit together.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Yeah, well, and I think that sometimes the best relationships

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: are when both people feel lucky to be with the other person.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Yes, exactly. It's balanced that way.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And then that's when you, in terms of jobs,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: in terms of going to the gym, all those kinds of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And yeah, so a little bit of jealousy.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: I have a discussion with those people.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: There's people in relationships where like, no, no, there's no...

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: They never experience jealousy.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: I wonder what that's like, because they're very successful relationships.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And I always wonder, you know, I'm currently single,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: so I always doubt that I know what the hell I'm doing at all.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: But I'm definitely somebody that experiences jealousy

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: and kind of enjoys jealousy, like a little bit of like missing.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: To me, that's like you're missing the other person.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: You're longing for the other person.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And here's another interesting wrinkle that I also talk about in the book

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: is sometimes people intentionally evoke jealousy in their partner.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And I think that's also a kind of testing of a bond kind of issue.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And especially women, but I think both sexes interpret a total absence of jealousy

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: as a sign that their partner is not sufficiently committed to them

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: or sufficiently in love with them.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: So if you like to say, I don't know, if you go to a party with your partner

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: and then you leave the room for some reason, you come back

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: and your partner is passionately kissing someone else and doesn't bother you at all,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: that might be a cue to the partner that, well, maybe you're not very in love with that person

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: or not very committed to them.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And so...

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: So it's a good way to test.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: That said, I mean, I love the term meat poaching, by the way.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: I believe here in Texas, meat poaching is officially illegal.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: of I guess for meat poaching, for meat switching,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: performed by the partner and then the frustration and the anger that's resulting.

body.input: I always wondered why the violence is directed towards the partner

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: versus the person who did the other male.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: It tends to be evenly split.

body.input: So sometimes, and that's, I mean, men especially,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: when someone poaches on their mate, they have homicidal fantasies.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Towards which...

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Well, toward the mate poacher, yeah, but equally split.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: So I think the non-lethal violence tends to be more directed toward the mate

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: because it's...and this is a horrible thing of male sexual psychology,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: but I think part of the violence is functional in the sense that it's designed to

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: keep a mate and prevent her from engaging in anything with other potential mate poachers.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: But people do.

body.input: So even...it goes back to the French law,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: and shot him, that was viewed as a crime of passion.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: It's still not legal, but you kind of get a discount for it.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Whereas if he goes home, thinks about it for a while,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: then gets the gun and comes back, then that's premeditated murder.

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: See, to me, I guess everybody's different.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: To me, I have zero anger towards the partner in that situation.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: To me, because that's definitive proof of the solitude.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: So like why...what's the function of the anger there?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: To me, all of my anger is towards the guy, the poacher.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Because some of it has to do probably with the status establishing.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: I want to reestablish, at least in my own mind, the formidability.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And that seems to be...I guess we're all different,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: but maybe because I roll around with guys a lot, like grapple and wrestling, all that kind of stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: To me, to establish status is competing with other males, not with the female.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Because that's a break of loyalty.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: What's the point of anger at this point? That's just betrayal.

body.input: Well, except that a lot of the mate poaching is discovered,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: or accused to mate poaching are discovered before the consummation of the act.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: So it might be just...
