metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Or mild flirtation, things like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: So the violence is designed to head off the threat before it becomes real.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Boy, aren't human relations, especially romantic ones, complicated?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Very. But that's what makes them so fascinating to study.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Yes, exactly. From a science perspective and to study from within,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: like Richard Wrangham with the chimps, be in it.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Study from the end of one perspective.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: What do you make of polyamory?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: So what the heck is...what do you make of marriage?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: What are your thoughts about marriage? What are your thoughts about lifelong monogamy?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: What's your thoughts about polyamory, given that we've been talking about ideas of mate switching and poaching and all that kind of stuff?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: I think that we evolved to be, I prefer the term, a pair-bonded species.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: So pair bonding is one of the strategies.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Pair-bonded long-term mating is one of the strategies.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: But that doesn't necessarily mean for decades and decades or lifelong,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: because we often pair bond serially.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: So we get into a relationship that might last a year or five years and then break up and then form another relationship.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: So we engage in serial mating. We engage in infidelity.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: We engage in some short-term mating.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And so we have what I describe as a menu of mating strategies.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And which particular mating strategy an individual adopts depends on a wide variety of factors.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: I think some are just kind of personal proclivities.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Some depend on your mate value.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: So if you are an 8, a 9, or a 10, you have more options for what mating strategy you want to pursue.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: If you're a 1 or a 2, you're not going to be able to be polyamorous in a likelihood.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: There's a lot of attention to polyamory now.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And it's unclear whether there's an increase in it or whether people are just talking about it more.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: It is the case, and I know several people who are in polyamorous relationships,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: and I've talked with them in detail about them.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And jealousy is often a factor in that.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And they describe it as kind of like an emotion that has to be somehow tamed or dealt with in some way.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And so in polyamory, there are many different types of polyamory.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And one type, for example, is you have a primary love partner and then some others on the side that are permitted,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: usually within, in consensual terms, within an explicit contract that the primary partners work out.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: So it's OK if you, you know, I know it's one couple, it's OK if you do it outside the city limits of Los Angeles, but not within.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Some say it's OK for Thursday, but I want the weekend, the Friday and Saturday nights to me.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: It's OK if there's sexual involvement, but no emotional involvement.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: So there are different strategies that people work out, and some of them are designed to try to keep jealousy at bay.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: So I think it's an evolved emotion that is a natural emotion that people experience.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Now, interestingly, there's a while we're on this topic, there's a sex difference therein,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: namely, if you contrast sexual jealousy with emotional jealousy or sexual infidelity with emotional infidelity.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And so we in one set of studies, I put my participants or we used to call them subjects into this,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: what I call the Sophie's choice of the jealousy dilemmas.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: I said, imagine your partner became interested in someone else and you discover that they have had passionate sexual intercourse with this person

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: and they've gotten emotionally involved with them, they've fallen in love with them.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Which aspect of the infidelity upsets you more?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And when you, that's why I call it the Sophie's choice, both terrible choices.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: But men much more likely to say the sexual infidelity is what upsets me.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: More women, it's like, why are you even asking me? It's a no brainer.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: 85% of the women say the emotional infidelity is what bothers them more.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Former student of mine, Barry Cooley did a really interesting study of analysis of this reality show called Cheaters.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: I've actually never seen it, but where if you suspect your partner of cheating,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: then the detective from the TV team will follow the person and then they'll call up and say,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: we've just seen, you found your husband here in the motel, do you want to come down and talk to him?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And so what he analyzed though was the verbal interrogations that people had when they confronted their partner.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And women wanted to know, are you in love with her?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Men wanted to know, did you fuck him or did you have sex with him?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And so it's this sex difference in sensitivity to these different cues of infidelity.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And of course, there's an evolutionary logic to this sex difference.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And it's been replicated, not the Cheaters study, but the hypothetical Sophie's choice study has been replicated now in Sweden and China.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: It's a universal sex difference.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: So given that sex difference, and you mentioned another one to just return to, which is in the engineering disciplines.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Yeah, person thing orientation.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: So until I started to see writing about it in the sort of psychology literature, I observed this anecdotally a lot.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And the reason I observed it is I was confused.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: So I care a lot about robots. I'm a robotics person.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And so a lot of males in the robotics community really didn't care about what's called the human robot interaction problem,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: which is like robots when they interact with humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And then a lot of females, all brilliant in the robotics community, cared about the human robot interaction.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: They cared about the human, what the robot called communicates with the human in the picture, human in the loop.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And I was really confused, like, because the difference to me in my anecdotal interactions, but the end is quite large there.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Like I, you know, I'm in the robotics community. I know a lot of people.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And I was confused because for me, I really care about human robot interaction.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: I see I care about both a lot.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And in the same thing here in terms of emotional cheating versus physical cheating, I care a lot about both.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And I have like this oscillating brain. So I wonder what that says about my brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: So I often wonder this because there's specific sex differences that are represented in the data and the literature.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And I seem to oscillate depending on mood.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And I wonder what that says about me. Why do I care so much about that robot on the floor?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: I care not half. I care about how it works and the other half how it makes other people feel.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Yeah. What is that?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Yeah. So I guess what I would say, this gets back to our earlier discussion of agency and communion,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: where I actually think that it's a sign of being well balanced to have both capacities within you.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And so you get people who are unimodal or they just have one mode of operating.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Let's say it's the thing mode, which engineers tend to be good at.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: You have to be good at it to be a good engineer because things have to actually work.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: It's not in some dream or hypothetical state things have to have to actually work.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: But with the agency and communion, I think it's good to have a balance.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And that's why I think some of the best romantic relationships are those where people are,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: they're high on what they used to call androgyny, where they have both the positive features of agency and communion,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: the positive features of masculinity and femininity within the same mix,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: but also with the footnote of not the unmitigated agency or unmitigated communion, both of which can be negative.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And so I view these as capacities and some people are out of balance.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Some people have a good balance between the two.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: It sounds like you have a good balance between the two.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Well, but also the allocation. I feel like it's a very dynamic thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: It's like, at least where for me personally, of the beauty between humans, of the dance, of the push and pull, of the different moods.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: It's like a dynamical system. It's not two static entities fully represented and consistent through every interaction.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Sometimes people might confuse the fact that I often talk about love and I love humans, that I don't have a temper,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: that I don't have like, I lose my shit all the time, especially like on things I really am passionate about, like people I work with and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: I'm all over the place. But underneath it, there's a deep love and respect for humans, but like I lose my shit all the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And that chaos, that roller coaster, I think that's what makes human relations awesome.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: I mean, the push and pull of it, of course, it can oscillate too far, which is when it becomes Amber Heard type of situation,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: when it turns to emotional or physical violence, when it turns to jealousy, crosses a line where it's hurtful.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And it crosses that vast gray landscape of what is abuse versus what is just beautiful turmoil of human nature.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And it's complicated.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Yeah, it's complicated and it's dynamic. And I would just add to that, I thought you phrased that brilliantly, but I would just add to that.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: It also depends on sort of what you're trying to do. And so I think some of the oscillation can be what task, what problem you're trying to solve.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And so if you're, I don't know, trying to build a bridge or something, you need to be very thing oriented and make sure the damn thing actually works and doesn't collapse when a car goes over it.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: If you're trying to form a relationship and you're entirely thing oriented, it's not going to work.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And that's one of the people, one of the things with males tend to be more on the so-called spectrum side of things where one of the hallmarks is a deficit in social mind reading.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Just to add to your point about, I guess I've already made it, that of the dynamic properties of the roller coaster is depending on what problem you're trying to solve, you might want to toggle back and forth to one pole or the other.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: You wrote a book called Why Women Have Sex, Understanding Sexual Motivations from Adventure to Revenge. That sounds fun. And everything in between. So why do women have sex?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Well, I co-wrote it with a female who's Cindy Meston, a wonderful friend and colleague and co-author and co-collaborator.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: I wouldn't be presumptuous enough to write a book called Why Women Have Sex by myself as a male.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Did you contribute anything to this book? I'm just kidding.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: I did, but I have to tell you a story about the origins of this idea, which I give credit to Cindy Meston for.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And she's a colleague in the psychology department with me and we would go out to dinner once a week or so and we were just talking about that. She raised this issue.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And so we started to brainstorm. Originally it was Why Humans Have Sex. And that's the scientific article we published was Why Humans, because we're interested in males and females.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And so I said, I would come up, well, they have sex because of X. And then Cindy Meston would come up, she'd say, oh, here are seven other reasons.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And I'd come up with one more and she'd come up with another seven. So she's in some sense, importantly, the originator or fountain of this idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Oh, so she's able, there's something about the way she thinks about sexuality that's able to deeply introspect about reasons for sex.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Yeah, and probably especially about female sexuality. And this is one of the interesting things and why it's so fun for me to collaborate with, in this case, female,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: because they do have a different sexual psychology than males. And I've noticed this, that's why in my graduate studies, I've had 30 or so PhD students, about half of them male, half of them female.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And the women come up with different questions, different scientific questions that I wouldn't have thought of necessarily. And so anyway, so it turned out to be a good collaboration.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: I will say that we co-wrote it and that I did contribute to it. And especially the evolutionary insights.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: So is there a good few words you can say to why women have sex? What are some primary motivations?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Well, we originally came up with a list of 237 reasons for why humans have sex. And they range from some of the obvious ones, because it feels good,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: because I wanted to relieve stress, to relieve menstrual cramps, to get rid of a headache, to get my boyfriend off my back so I could get some work done.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: So things like that to others, like, here's another one, so that he'd take out the damn garbage.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: But another one, it was kind of interesting that someone, one nomination was to get closer to God. So there were some that were kind of spiritual motivations for having sex.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And then some of the nastier ones like to get revenge on my partner or to get revenge on a rival. So that's sleeping with my rival's boyfriend.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: So there's some nasty stuff and some good stuff in there.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: It's so fascinating because, yeah, sex has such a powerful role in our psychology, but also in our culture.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: So you can make significant statements in the status hierarchy about the selection of your sexual partner.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: It's interesting. So it's not just because you're horny. It's all those other kinds of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Yeah, well, hornyness is one, but there are other reasons.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: What about different kinds of sex? So, you know, what's, again, this is not the Humor in the Lab podcast. Rough sex versus, quote, making love.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: What's the explanation between all of that? All the various kinks? Now, that's just a basic sort of split, but all the different kinks that humans establish, all the different fantasies and all those kinds of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Yeah. Well, that's a complicated question for which I don't think we have sufficient time to get into that in detail.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And it is complicated because there are some sexual fantasies that, sexual fantasies, by the way, I think are a really fascinating window into our sexual psychology,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: because in a way they're unconstrained by things like rules and norms in society and cultural presses that you're kind of free to fantasize about whatever you want to fantasize about.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: So I think it provides an interesting window into human sexuality. And there are some predictable ones.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And then there are some also individual or idiosyncratic ones. And the again, there's a fundamental sex difference in this in that when you talk about like fetishes or like shoe fetishes, leather fetishes, different types of things,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: males are much more prone to those than females. Shoe fetish, you said? Foot fetishes? Almost all fetishes. Males are overrepresented.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And I think it's partly because there's some evidence that they're classically conditioned.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: So I think that first or early sexual experiences that people have kind of conditioned them to the cues that are present during those early ones. And so if your first sex experience happened to be, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: involved in visual images of shoes or you're having to look in your shoes when you first had sex,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: for example, or leather or zippers or whatever the case is, that people develop these very individualistic sexual turn-ons based on these early sexual experiences.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: So it could also be, you said have sex, but it could also be sexual feelings. Early sexual feelings.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Yeah. So I wonder what that is about men that they have a more, when they first start experiencing sexual feelings, that they're more sensitive to the cues and those cues somehow have a deep psychological effect on their development of their sexuality.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: So if they have kinks, that means they're somehow more cue sensitive and maybe, does a matter of society, like, slap someone on the wrist for it? Does that help solidify the kinks?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Yeah. I don't know about the society slapping on the wrist, but I think what it is is this, I think this is the evolutionary hypothesis anyway about why there's this sex difference.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And that is that men are conditioned to anything that's going to lead to sex. Because whereas women don't have to be, from a male perspective, because of women's greater investment, because the nine month pregnancy, etc.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: In order to reproduce, women have to invest this tremendous amount. Men don't. One act of sex can produce an offspring. And so for men, but not for women.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: And so this huge asymmetry in investment means that the payoff matrix of different sexual strategies differs for the sexes. In that context, women become the valuable and scarce resource over which men compete.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Anything that leads to successful sex is going to be selected for it. And so men are very sensitive to being sexually conditioned. That's what's called sexual conditioning, to whatever cues are associated with sex happening.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: From a woman's perspective, sex is not a scarce resource. So a woman could go out here in Austin any night or probably any day on 6th Street and have no problem having sex with a guy within 10 minutes.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Okay. Guy would have more difficulty. He's not going to go out, unless he's Johnny Depp or really, really charming.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: Yeah. Yeah, that's a fascinating dimorphism or asymmetry in our mate selection. What do you think is the effect on this young male brain, a female too, of pornography?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: So one of the fascinating things that the digital world brought us now, I grew up at a time when like a magazine, like a Victoria's Secret magazine was like my source of sexual inspiration.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: But that was before the internet. And now the internet with pornography makes it extremely accessible. All kinds of kinks, all kinds of wild variety. I mean, variety and quantity is immense.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Buss: Sex, Dating, Relationships, and Sex Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #282

body.input: So what do you think that has, how that affects mate selection, mating, and just the human psychology of the two sexes of the species?

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: So we all agreed about what the endpoints had to be.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: And you wondered, why are there 30,000 participants in each of these trials?

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: That's because of ACTIVE's group mapping out what the power needed to be

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: for this to be convincing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: Same with therapeutics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: We have run at least 20 therapeutic agents through trials

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: that ACTIVE supported in record time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: That's how we got monoclonal antibodies that we know work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: That would not have been possible if I didn't already have a sense

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: of how to work with the private sector that came out of AMP.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: AMP took two years to get started.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: ACTIVE took two weeks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: We just kept the lawyers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: Wow, to get 100 people over.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: Yeah, kept the lawyers out of the room.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: Now you're going to get yourself in trouble.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: So I do hope one day the story of this incredible vaccine,

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: development of vaccine protocols and trials and all this kind of details,

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: the messy, beautiful details of science and engineering

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: that led to the manufacturing, the deployment and the scientific testing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: It's such a nice dance between engineering and the space of manufacture of the vaccines.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: You start before the studies are complete, you start making the vaccines

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: just in case if the studies prove to be positive, then you can start deploying them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: Just like so many parties, like you said, private and public playing together,

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: that's just a beautiful dance that is one of the, for me, the sources of hope

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: in this very tricky time where there's a lot of things to be cynical about

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: in terms of the games politicians play and the hardship experienced

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: of the economy and all those kinds of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: But to me, this dance of vaccine development was done just beautifully

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: and it gives me hope.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: It does me as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: And it was in many ways the finest hour that science has had in a long time

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: being called upon when every day counted and making sure that time was not wasted.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: And things were done rigorously but quickly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: So you're incredibly good as the leader of the NIH.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: It seems like you're having a heck of a lot of fun.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: Why step down from this role after so much fun?

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: Well, no other NIH director has served more than one president

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: after being appointed by one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: You're sort of done.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: And the idea of being carried over for a second presidency with Trump

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: and now a third one with Biden is unheard of.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: I just think, Lex, that scientific organizations benefit from new vision.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: And 12 years is a really long time to have the same leader.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: And if I wasn't going to stick it out for the entire Biden four-year term,

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: it's good not to wait too late during that to signal an intent to step down

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: because the president's got to find the right person, got to nominate them,

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: got to get the Senate to confirm them, which is an unpredictable process right now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: And you don't want to try to do that in the second half of somebody's term as president.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: This has got to happen now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: So I kind of decided back at the end of May that this should be my final year.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: And I'm OK with that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: I do have some mixed emotions because I love the NIH.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: I love the job.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: It's exhausting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: I'm traditionally for the last 20 months anyway working 100 hours a week.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: It's just that's what it takes to juggle all of this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: And that keeps me from having a lot of time for anything else.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: And I wouldn't mind because I don't think I'm done yet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: I wouldn't mind having some time to really think about what the next chapter should be.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: And I have none of that time right now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: Do I have another calling?

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: Is there something else I could contribute that's different than this?

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: I'd like to find that out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: I think the right answer is you're just stepping down to focus on your music career.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: That might not be a good plan for anything very sustainable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: But I think that is a sign of a great leader as George Washington did stepping down at the right time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: Ted Williams.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: He quit when I think he hit a home run on his last at bat and his average was 400 at the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: No one to walk away.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: I mean, it's hard, but it's beautiful to see in a leader.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: You also oversaw the Human Genome Project.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: You mentioned the Brain Initiative, which has, you know, it's a dream to map the human brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: And there's the dream to map the human code, which was the Human Genome Project.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: And you have said that it is humbling for me and awe-inspiring to realize that we have caught the first glimpse of our own instruction book, previously known only to God.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: How does that, if you can just kind of wax poetic for a second, how does it make you feel that we were able to map this instruction book, look into our own code and be able to reverse engineer it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: It's breathtaking.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: It's so fundamental.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: And yet, for all of human history, we're ignorant of the details of what that instruction book looked like.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: And then we crossed the bridge into the territory of the known.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: And we had that in front of us, still written in a language that we had to learn how to read.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: And we're in the process of doing that and will be for decades to come.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: But we owned it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: We had it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: And it has such profound consequences.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: It's both a book about our history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: It's a book of sort of the parts list of a human being, the genes that are in there and how they're regulated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: And it's also a medical textbook that can teach us things that will provide answers to illnesses we don't understand and alleviate suffering and premature death.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: So it's a pretty amazing thing to contemplate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: And it has utterly transformed the way we do science.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: And it is in the process of transforming the way we do medicine, although much of that still lies ahead.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: You know, while we were working on the Genome Project, it was sort of hard to get this sense of a wow-ness because it was just hard work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: And you were getting, you know, another megabase.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: OK, this is good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: But when did you actually step back and say, we did it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: It's the profoundness of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: I mean, there were two points, I guess.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: One was the announcement on that June 26, 2000, where the whole world heard, well, we don't quite have it, but we got a pretty good draft.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: And suddenly people are like realizing, oh, this is a big deal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: For me, it was more when we got the full analysis of it, published it in February 2001 in that issue of Nature paper that Eric Lander and Bob Waterston and I were the main authors.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: And we toiled over and tried to get as much insight as we could in there about what the meaning of all this was.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: But you also had this sense that we are such beginning readers here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: We are still in kindergarten trying to make sense out of this three billion letter book.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: And we're going to be at this for generations to come.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: You are a man of faith, Christian, and you are a man of science.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: What is the role of religion and of science in society and in the individual human mind and heart like yours?

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: Well, I was not a person of faith when I was growing up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: I became a believer in my 20s, influenced as a medical student by a recognition that I hadn't really thought through the issues of what's the meaning of life?

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: Why are we all here? What happens when you die? Is there a God?

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: Science is not so helpful in answering those questions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: So I had to look around in other places and ultimately came to my own conclusion that atheism, which is where I had been, was the least supportable of the choices because it was the assertion of a universal negative, which scientists aren't supposed to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: And agnosticism came as an attractive option, but felt a little bit like a cop out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: So I had to keep going, trying to figure out why do believers actually believe this stuff?

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: And came to realize it was all pretty compelling that there's no proof.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: I can't prove to you or anybody else that God exists, but I can say it's pretty darn plausible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: And ultimately, what kind of God is it caused me to search through various religions and see, well, what do people think about that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: And to my surprise, encountered the person of Jesus Christ as unique in every possible way and answering a lot of the questions I couldn't otherwise answer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: And somewhat kicking and screaming, I became a Christian, even though at the time, as a medical student already interested in genetics, people predicted my head would then explode because these were incompatible worldviews.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: They really have not been for me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: I am so fortunate, I think, that in a given day, wrestling with an issue, it can have both the rigorous scientific component and it can have the spiritual component.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: COVID-19 is a great example.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: These vaccines are both an amazing scientific achievement and an answer to prayer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: When I'm wrestling with vaccine hesitancy and trying to figure out what answers to come up with, I get so frustrated sometimes and I'm comforted by reassurances that God is aware of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: I don't have to do this alone.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: So I know there are people like your friend Sam Harris, who feel differently.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: Sam wrote a rather famous op-ed in the New York Times when I was nominated as the NIH director, saying, this is a terrible mistake.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: You can't have somebody who believes in God running the NIH.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: He's just going to completely ruin the place.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: I have a testimonial. Christopher Hitchens, a devout atheist, if I could say so, was a friend of yours and referred to you as, quote, one of the greatest living Americans and stated that you are one of the most devout believers he has ever met.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: He further stated that you were sequencing the genome of the cancer that would ultimately claim his life and that your friendship, despite their differing opinions on religion, was an example of the greatest armed truce in modern times.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: What did you learn from Christopher Hitchens about life or perhaps what is a fond memory you have of this man with whom you've disagreed, but who is also your friend?

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: Yeah, I loved Hitch.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: I'm sorry he's gone.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: Iron sharpens iron.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: There's nothing better for trying to figure out where you are with your own situation and your own opinions, your own worldviews, than encountering somebody who's completely in another space and who's got the gift, as Hitch did, of challenging everything and doing so over a glass of scotch or two or three.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: Yeah, we got off to a rough start where in an interaction we had at a rather highbrow dinner, he was really deeply insulting of a question I was asking.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: But, you know, I was like, okay, that's fine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: Let's figure out how we could have a more civil conversation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: And then I really learned to greatly admire his intellect and to find the jousting with him. And it wasn't all about faith, although it often was. It was really inspiring and innovating, energizing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: And then when he got cancer, I became sort of his ally, trying to help him find pathways through the various options and maybe helped him to stay around on this planet for an extra six months or so.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: And I have the warmest feelings of being in his apartment downtown over a glass of wine, talking about whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: Sometimes it was science. He was fascinated by science. Sometimes it was Thomas Jefferson. Sometimes it was faith. And I knew it would always be really interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: So he's now gone.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: Do you think about your own mortality? Are you afraid of death?

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: I'm not afraid. I'm not looking forward to it. I don't want to rush it because I feel like I got some things I can still do here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: But as a person of faith, I don't think I'm afraid. I'm 71. I know I don't have an infinite amount of time left.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: And I want to use the time I've got in some sort of way that matters.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: I'm not ready to become a full time golfer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: But I don't quite know what that is. I do feel that I've had a chance to do amazingly powerful things as far as experiences. And maybe God has something else in mind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: I wrote this book 16 years ago, The Language of God, about science and faith, trying to explain how, from my perspective, these are compatible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: These are in harmony. They're complementary if you are careful about which kind of question you're asking.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: And to my surprise, a lot of people seem to be interested in that. They were tired of hearing the extreme voices like Dawkins at one end,

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: and people like Ken Ham and Answers in Genesis on the other end saying, if you trust science, you're going to hell.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: And they thought there must be a way that these things could get along. And that's what I tried to put forward.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: And then I started a foundation, BioLogos, which then I had to step away from to become NIH director, which has just flourished, maybe because I stepped away.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: I don't know. But it now has millions of people who come to that website, and they run amazing meetings.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: And I think a lot of people have really come to a sense that this is OK. I can love science and I can love God. And that's not a bad thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: So maybe there's something more I can do in that space. Maybe that book is ready for a second edition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: I think so. But when you look back, life is finite. What do you hope your legacy is?

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: I don't know. This whole legacy thing is a little bit hard to embrace. It feels a little self-promoting, doesn't it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: I sort of feel like in many ways I went to my own funeral on October 5th when I announced that I was stepping down and I got the most amazing responses from people,

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: some of whom I knew really well, some of whom I didn't know at all, who were just telling me stories about something that I had contributed to that made a difference to them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: And that was incredibly heartwarming. And that's enough. I don't want to build an edifice.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: I don't have a plan for a monument or a statue. God help us. I do feel like I've been incredibly fortunate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: I've had the chance to play a role in things that were pretty profound from the Genome Project to NIH, to COVID vaccines.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: And I ought to be plenty satisfied that I've had enough experiences here to feel pretty good about the way in which my life panned out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: We did a bunch of difficult questions in this conversation. Let me ask the most difficult one, that perhaps is the reason you turned to God. What is the meaning of life?

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: Have you figured it out yet?

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: You expect me to put that into three sentences?

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: We only have a couple of minutes. At least hurry up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: Well, that's not a question that I think science helps me with. So you're going to push me into the phase zone, which is where I'd want to go with that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: I think, well, what is the meaning? Why are we here? What do we put here to do?

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: I do believe we're here for just a blink of an eye and that our existence somehow goes on beyond that in a way that I don't entirely understand, despite efforts to do so.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: I think we are called upon in this blink of an eye to try to make the world a better place, to try to love people, to try to do a better job of our more altruistic instincts and less of our selfish instincts,

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: to try to be what God calls us to be, people who are holy, not people who are driven by self-indulgence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: And sometimes I'm better at that than others. But I think that for me as a Christian is a pretty clear. I mean, it's to live out the Sermon on the Mount.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: Once I read that, I couldn't unread it. All those Beatitudes, all the blessings. That's what we're supposed to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: And the meaning of life is to strive for that standard, recognizing you're going to fail over and over again and that God forgives you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: Hopefully to put a little bit of love out there into the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: That's what it's about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: Francis, I'm truly humbled and inspired by both your brilliance and your humility and that you would spend your extremely valuable time with me today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: It was really an honor. Thank you so much for talking today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: I was glad too. And you asked a really good question. So your reputation as the best podcaster has borne itself out here this afternoon.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: Thank you so much.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: Thanks for listening to this conversation with Francis Collins. To support this podcast, please check out our sponsors in the description.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: And now let me leave you with some words from Isaac Newton, reflecting on his life and work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: I seem to have been only like a boy, playing on the seashore and diverting myself and now and then finding a smoother pebble or prettier shell than ordinary, whilst the great ocean of truth lay all undiscovered before me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Francis Collins: National Institutes of Health (NIH) | Lex Fridman Podcast #238

body.input: Thank you for listening and hope to see you next time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ronald Sullivan: The Ideal of Justice in the Face of Controversy and Evil | Lex Fridman Podcast #170

metadata.title: Podcast: Ronald Sullivan: The Ideal of Justice in the Face of Controversy and Evil | Lex Fridman Podcast #170

body.input: most of my time is teaching and writing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ronald Sullivan: The Ideal of Justice in the Face of Controversy and Evil | Lex Fridman Podcast #170

body.input: But I tend to take cases that most deem to be impossible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ronald Sullivan: The Ideal of Justice in the Face of Controversy and Evil | Lex Fridman Podcast #170

body.input: I take the challenging sorts of cases.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ronald Sullivan: The Ideal of Justice in the Face of Controversy and Evil | Lex Fridman Podcast #170

body.input: in the public had the case pre-judged,

body.input: even though the specific allegations did not regard

body.input: any of the people in the New Yorker.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ronald Sullivan: The Ideal of Justice in the Face of Controversy and Evil | Lex Fridman Podcast #170

body.input: everything that was going on allegedly with Harvey.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ronald Sullivan: The Ideal of Justice in the Face of Controversy and Evil | Lex Fridman Podcast #170

body.input: So I decided to take the case and I did.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ronald Sullivan: The Ideal of Justice in the Face of Controversy and Evil | Lex Fridman Podcast #170

body.input: Is there a philosophy behind you taking

metadata.title: Podcast: Ronald Sullivan: The Ideal of Justice in the Face of Controversy and Evil | Lex Fridman Podcast #170

metadata.title: Podcast: Ronald Sullivan: The Ideal of Justice in the Face of Controversy and Evil | Lex Fridman Podcast #170

body.input: Yeah, I do.

body.input: I'd like to take on hard cases and I like to take on

metadata.title: Podcast: Ronald Sullivan: The Ideal of Justice in the Face of Controversy and Evil | Lex Fridman Podcast #170

body.input: the cases that are with unpopular defenses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ronald Sullivan: The Ideal of Justice in the Face of Controversy and Evil | Lex Fridman Podcast #170

body.input: That are with unpopular defendants, unpopular clients.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ronald Sullivan: The Ideal of Justice in the Face of Controversy and Evil | Lex Fridman Podcast #170

body.input: And with respect to the latter,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ronald Sullivan: The Ideal of Justice in the Face of Controversy and Evil | Lex Fridman Podcast #170

body.input: that's where Harvey Weinstein fell.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ronald Sullivan: The Ideal of Justice in the Face of Controversy and Evil | Lex Fridman Podcast #170

body.input: It's because we need lawyers and good lawyers

metadata.title: Podcast: Ronald Sullivan: The Ideal of Justice in the Face of Controversy and Evil | Lex Fridman Podcast #170
